messages:
alice: Quick heads-up — we're deferring the regional cutover originally scheduled for tomorrow 02:00 UTC. Reason: an unexpected compatibility regression in the quota router that affects Dedicated traffic routing.
ben: Ack. Is this a rollback or a temporary hold on the cutover window?
alice: Temporary hold. We're going to clear the canary buckets, run a compatibility patch, and re-run the small-region soak for 6 hours before we consider rescheduling. No wide rollback yet. :warning:
dana: ETA for the patch? I want to update customer success for any potential impact to reserved capacity customers.
alice: Ben and Carla are on the patch. Expect a PR and canary patch deploy within 45–60 minutes. Carla will run the validation testset.
carla: Pushing a patch now. I'll post the canary job output here when ready.
devops-bot: deploy-begin alice/patch/quota-router v2.3.1-canary -> infra-canary-1
oncall: Noted. I'll hold the canary monitoring window and keep the oncall rotation ready if latency/error spikes occur.
carla: Canary deploy done. Logs: ```
2026-03-23T14:20:12Z canary: accepted
2026-03-23T14:20:50Z healthcheck: ok
2026-03-23T14:22:03Z routing-tests: 292/300 pass
```
carla: Two failing integration checks reproducible locally — looks like a header mismatch for multi-tenant tokens. Investigating.
ben: If it's token header ordering, we can hotpatch the parser with a defensive shim and keep the window. Green or go/no-go in ~30m?
alice: Let's prioritize safety. If Carla confirms the shim fixes >99% of routing paths in canary, we'll convert this to a staged rollout (10% -> 50% -> full) with a 1h soak per stage. If not, we hold and schedule the full cutover for next Tuesday.
dana: I'll send a short note to CS + Sales: \"Cutover deferred; potential reschedule next Tue; customers on Dedicated unaffected for now but we are monitoring.\" Want me to include a mitigation ETA?
alice: Please include: patch in progress, canary validation ongoing, ETA 2–4h for decision.
oncall: Alert thresholds set: latency +20%, error-rate >0.5% for 10m. If triggered, automatic rollback to previous canary image.
ben: Quick checklist for the staged rollout if patch passes: 1) bump canary to 10% (infra API), 2) wait 1h soak; 3) 50% ramp; 4) 1h soak; 5) full roll. Who will own the ramp ops?
alice: Ben owns ramps, Carla owns validation tests, Oncall handles monitoring/rollback. Dana will handle comms.
carla: Validation tests with broader headers added — running now. Expect results in ~20m.
dana: Sent CS/Sales PSA with the suggested wording and ETA. Link: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/CC-1234 (internal tracking). :email:
carla: Validation update: 10k synthetic requests over 30m, 99.6% pass. The shim drops the failing header when absent and normalizes ordering. I recommend staged rollout.
alice: Good. Ben, start the 10% ramp now. Post ramp numbers in this thread.
ben: Kicking off ramp. infra-cli: ```
infra ramp --service quota-router --percent 10 --from canary-1
```
devops-bot: ramp-event id=rv-7621 percent=10 service=quota-router status=started
ben: Ramp completed. Initial metrics (5m): latency +3%, errors 0.08%. No alerts.
oncall: Monitoring: no threshold breaches so far. I'll keep 15m heartbeat updates.
dana: Updating CS Slack channel and the customer-facing status page (note: no customer-facing outages).
alice: Thanks everyone. If all stays green, we follow the plan to 50% in 1h. If any threshold is hit, roll back and we regroup. :thumbsup:
ben: 1h checkpoint scheduled at 15:35 UTC — will post results here.
carla: FYI — added an automated regression test to the preflight pipeline to catch header-order issues going forward. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/quota-router/pull/789
dana: Noted. I'll include that in the postmortem action items so CS can reference the long-term fix.
alice: Closing loop — no customer impact expected. Will post a short postmortem after the release completes. Thanks all. :party:
